title: dassi — Teach It Once. It Works For You.
byline: jwax33 — extracting structured data out of a Roll20 journal
excerpt: Teach dassi how you do a job once and it keeps doing it — on your schedule, in the web apps you're already signed into, with the approvals you set.
content_html:
Do it once.
Then stop doing it.

01 Teach it

Walk it through the job once — in plain English.

02 Set the rules

Which sites, what schedule, what needs your OK.

03 Let it run

It works on schedule while your browser is open. You handle only the exceptions.

Three jobs worth teaching dassi first.

Swipe →

Reconcile payouts against orders

Screen applicants, update the ATS

Weekly report, built while you sleep

In your browser.
On your side.

Runs in the Chrome you already use

Uses the accounts you're signed into — no integrations

Your session stays yours — it pauses for your OK on the actions you flag

Repeat runs cost less — dassi keeps tuning the job each time it runs, and caches context within a run

Learned site skills — dassi writes itself a JavaScript library per site, so it calls a function instead of re-reading the page

Do it once. Then stop doing it.

dassi isn't a genie that already knows your job. It's closer to a new hire who's good at the web and needs one walkthrough of how you do things.

01 Teach it

Describe the job in plain English, or walk dassi through it once while it watches. It reads the pages you're logged into, so there's no context to paste in and no integration to wire up.

02 Set the rules

Choose the sites it uses, what changes each time, when it runs, where the result goes, and which actions it has to ask you about first.

03 Let it run

Trigger it yourself or let the schedule fire. dassi tells you when it's done — or when it hits something only you can decide. You handle the exceptions, not the job.

Read docs

Three jobs worth teaching dassi first.

Not a gallery of everything possible. These are the shapes that keep coming back: something to reconcile, something to check, something to file — every week, inside apps only you can log into.

E-commerce

Reconcile payouts against orders

Runs
Every Friday at 9:00am, or on demand

Uses
Your store admin · marketplace payout reports · your sheet

You get
A row per order, with every mismatch flagged and the amount at stake beside it

Asks first
Before it opens a support case or messages a marketplace

Example result 142 orders checked · 139 matched · 3 exceptions left for you

See how it works →

Recruiting

Screen new applicants and update the ATS

Runs
Every weekday at 8:00am, or on demand

Uses
Your ATS · the job-board inbox · candidate profiles

You get
Each new applicant scored against your criteria, with the notes written back into the ATS

Asks first
Before it emails a candidate or moves anyone to rejected

Example result 26 applicants screened · 4 shortlisted · 2 unclear, left for you

See how it works →

Back office

Build the weekly report before you're awake

Runs
Every Monday at 7:00am, or on demand

Uses
Your dashboards · admin portals · Sheets or Excel

You get
Last week's numbers in your own template, with the moves worth noticing called out

Asks first
Before it sends anything to anyone

Example result 6 sources pulled · 1 dashboard wouldn't load, flagged for you

See how it works →

Built for work that comes back.

Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are excellent assistants, and each can drive a browser now. dassi does the job in the browser you already use, on the accounts you're already signed into, with the model you choose — and it still owns the job next Friday.

A general assistant A dassi workflow

One company's model Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model, switchable anytime

You ask for a task, right now dassi keeps the job on its books

One answer, in one chat A run history you can go back through

You watch it work It runs on schedule and brings you the exceptions

Correct it once, not every time.

When dassi gets something wrong — the wrong supplier, the wrong column, the wrong tone — tell it. The correction goes into a memory you and dassi can both read and edit, so it carries into the next run instead of dying in the chat.

How it works

The second run should cost a fraction of the first.

Most of what a browser agent spends goes on two things: re-reading pages it has already read, and working out how a site is put together every single time. dassi is built to stop paying for both.

Caching

Within a run, dassi keeps the job's context byte-stable, so every step after the first reads it from your model provider's cache — up to 90% off input tokens on Claude. You pay for that context once per run, not on every step.

Learned site skills

As dassi works a site, it writes itself a small JavaScript library for that site. From then on it calls a function instead of re-deriving selectors from screenshots and HTML — the cheap part of the stack doing what the expensive part used to.

And dassi keeps tuning a job each time it runs, so work you repeat gets cheaper the longer you keep it.

Use Claude, GPT, Gemini, or another model inside dassi, with your own key or included credits. The model is the engine; the workflow is the thing you keep.

Works where you already work.

dassi runs in the Chrome, Edge, or Brave you already use, on the sites and accounts you're already signed into. There's nothing to integrate, no API to request, and no new browser to adopt. If you can do the job in a tab, dassi can be taught to do it.

Bring Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, or anything on OpenRouter — your own key or dassi's included credits, switchable anytime.

Your browser session stays yours.

A workflow that runs without you only works if you trust where it runs and where it stops.

[*]Browser actions run on your machine. Your configured AI provider processes the instructions and website content needed to decide what to do next.

[*]It works on the accounts you're already signed into — no passwords to hand over, no credentials stored, no logins copied anywhere.

[*]You set the rules — dassi pauses for the actions you flag and for anything it can't settle on its own. Approve in the side panel, or over Telegram when a scheduled run needs you and you're away from your desk.

[*]You pick the model. Requests go to your configured provider, or through dassi's relay when using managed credits. Optional remote MCP access stores task instructions and results on dassi's servers so your authorized AI app can retrieve them.

[*]No new browser — dassi works in the Chrome, Edge, or Brave you already use.

Learn more in our privacy policy.

dassi isn't a genie that already knows your job. It's closer to a new hire who's good at the web and needs one walkthrough of how you do things.

01 Teach it

Describe the job in plain English, or walk dassi through it once while it watches. It reads the pages you're logged into, so there's no context to paste in and no integration to wire up.

02 Set the rules

Choose the sites it uses, what changes each time, when it runs, where the result goes, and which actions it has to ask you about first.

03 Let it run

Trigger it yourself or let the schedule fire. dassi tells you when it's done — or when it hits something only you can decide. You handle the exceptions, not the job.

Read docs

Three jobs worth teaching dassi first.

Not a gallery of everything possible. These are the shapes that keep coming back: something to reconcile, something to check, something to file — every week, inside apps only you can log into.

Runs Every Friday at 9:00am, or on demand

Uses Your store admin · marketplace payout reports · your sheet

Built for work that comes back.

Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are excellent assistants, and each can drive a browser now. dassi does the job in the browser you already use, on the accounts you're already signed into, with the model you choose — and it still owns the job next Friday.

A general assistant A dassi workflow

One company's model Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model, switchable anytime

You ask for a task, right now dassi keeps the job on its books

One answer, in one chat A run history you can go back through

You watch it work It runs on schedule and brings you the exceptions

Correct it once, not every time.

When dassi gets something wrong — the wrong supplier, the wrong column, the wrong tone — tell it. The correction goes into a memory you and dassi can both read and edit, so it carries into the next run instead of dying in the chat.

它是如何运作的

The second run should cost a fraction of the first.

Most of what a browser agent spends goes on two things: re-reading pages it has already read, and working out how a site is put together every single time. dassi is built to stop paying for both.

缓存

Within a run, dassi keeps the job's context byte-stable, so every step after the first reads it from your model provider's cache — up to 90% off input tokens on Claude. You pay for that context once per run, not on every step.

Learned site skills

As dassi works a site, it writes itself a small JavaScript library for that site. From then on it calls a function instead of re-deriving selectors from screenshots and HTML — the cheap part of the stack doing what the expensive part used to.

And dassi keeps tuning a job each time it runs, so work you repeat gets cheaper the longer you keep it.

Use Claude, GPT, Gemini, or another model inside dassi, with your own key or included credits. The model is the engine; the workflow is the thing you keep.

Works where you already work.

dassi runs in the Chrome, Edge, or Brave you already use, on the sites and accounts you're already signed into. There's nothing to integrate, no API to request, and no new browser to adopt. If you can do the job in a tab, dassi can be taught to do it.

Bring Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, or anything on OpenRouter — your own key or dassi's included credits, switchable anytime.

Your browser session stays yours.

A workflow that runs without you only works if you trust where it runs and where it stops.
